items.text: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70–78 marketed range, and expanded the deal to about 980 million Class A shares from a planned 825 million, the AP reports. That raises roughly $81 billion, which the AP and CNBC describe as the largest IPO on record, ahead of SpaceX's roughly $75 billion in June. It values the company at about $1.5 trillion. Shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday, Nov 19. The AP notes that Anthropic is unprofitable on a GAAP basis, carries $6.2 billion of debt, and has signed about $900 billion in compute and infrastructure commitments.
items.notes: Some outlets give $81.3bn raised and others 'over $81bn'. The first trade had not happened at the time of writing (Nasdaq opens 15:30 Warsaw time).

items.text: The AP called the Alaska Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola on Tuesday evening (Alaska time). Late-counted ballots took her to about 50.1% of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice tabulation is needed, Alaska Public Media reports. She unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan. The AP says this was the last undecided Senate race of the midterms and leaves Democrats with a 56–44 majority after flipping nine GOP-held seats. Sullivan's campaign did not comment, after saying earlier it would wait for every legal vote to be counted and certified. State certification is slated for Nov 25.
items.notes: The call came after the Nov 18 log was compiled. NPR and NBC also report the win. Final certified totals are not yet published.

items.text: Minutes of the Oct 27–28 FOMC meeting, released Nov 18, show that 'almost all' officials judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate. XTB's summary of the minutes says a few officials floated a move larger than 25 basis points if inflation data disappoint. The Fed held rates at 3.75–4.00% in October, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favour of a hike. Reuters says almost all participants discussed the risk that AI investment returns could disappoint. Most noted that AI-related debt has grown fast through complex, opaque financing, and a few worried that exposure is concentrated in a small number of firms. Markets fully price a quarter-point hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting.
items.notes: The full minutes page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20261028.htm) could not be fetched. The rate range, dissents and the 'more than 25bp' detail come from XTB's summary, not the primary text.

items.text: The S&P 500 slipped about 0.2% to 7,323.63 on Wednesday, its fifth straight loss. The Dow fell 561 points (1.1%) to about 50,198 and the Nasdaq rose 0.4%, according to CNBC figures relayed by Stock Titan. Nvidia closed down about 2.9%: it rose pre-market after its blowout results but gave up the gain. Health insurers dragged the Dow, with UnitedHealth down about 10% and Humana about 13% on a second day of selling over CMS's proposed anti-fraud audit rule. Hawkish Fed minutes also weighed on stocks.
items.notes: Closing levels are CNBC's 5:13 pm ET figures as relayed by Stock Titan.

items.text: CMS has proposed a broad anti-fraud rule called CRUSH (Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare), covering Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP and the ACA marketplace. The agency projects nearly $90 billion in federal savings over 2027–2036. Its centrepiece expands Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment (RADV) audits: findings from sampled records would be extrapolated across whole contracts back to payment year 2018, with no fee-for-service adjustment. CMS estimates recoveries of about $9 billion per payment year. The rule also tightens provider enrolment, broker oversight and overpayment-return deadlines, and comments are due Jan 19, 2027. Insurer stocks fell sharply on Nov 17–18, and analysts quoted by Beinsure expect legal challenges, since a court vacated an earlier RADV rule in 2025.
items.notes: Proposed around Nov 16, and only the market reaction falls in the window. The CMS primary text and Federal Register citation were not retrieved.

items.text: Sens. Maria Cantwell (D) and Mike Rounds (R) wrote to Jay Clayton, who chairs the White House Super Intelligence Task Force, warning that AI-enabled cyber threats are escalating faster than US defences. They asked for urgent protection of critical infrastructure and banks, faster rollout of AI defensive tools, and security standards for autonomous AI agents, Reuters reports. They cited a run of recent disruptions: a 24-hour Microsoft outage, the FAA ground stop, a United Airlines halt and a JPMorgan Chase processing bug. A day earlier, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CNBC he was '98% certain' none of these was a cyberattack and blamed new technology layered on ageing systems. Reuters adds that the FAA has tied its ground stop to a single router at a remote Arkansas facility.
items.notes: Mullin's remarks were made on Nov 17. The Arkansas router detail comes from Reuters (Shepardson), while CBS earlier pointed to old Cisco routers. The two are consistent, but the FAA's final root cause is still not published.

items.text: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission released its 2026 annual report to Congress on Nov 18. Its themes include control of the 'AI tech stack' and China's use of data. TokenPost says the commission recommends penalties for companies that fail to report use of Chinese AI models, SEC risk disclosures for listed firms, and a bar on Chinese models in critical infrastructure and national-security uses without a security review. Separately, Reuters reported (via U.S. News) that the Treasury and the White House OSTP have discussed requiring US companies to list on their websites the Chinese models they use, without banning them. The proposal is still under discussion.
items.notes: The recommendations come from secondary coverage, because the report PDF was not reviewed. The Reuters exclusive on the administration's deliberations could not be fetched directly, and its details come from TokenPost and the headline.

items.text: Trump landed in Shenzhen on Nov 18 after the Manila leg. PBS NewsHour reports that Xi Jinping greeted him personally at the airport, a first for a foreign leader in Xi's 14 years in power, and that Putin was also there. The first-ever formal trilateral of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders is set for Nov 19 on the APEC sidelines, alongside a third Trump–Xi bilateral this year and separate Trump–Putin talks. No official agenda has been released. Trump wants a three-way nuclear arms-control deal, which officials and analysts say has low prospects. Iran, Ukraine, trade and AI are also expected to come up.
items.notes: An NBC live-blog headline says Trump sat down with Putin ahead of the three-way talks, but the page could not be read. The summit's outcomes were not available at the time of writing.

items.text: At a state luncheon hosted by President Marcos in Manila on Nov 18, Trump said the US and the Philippines had concluded 'the biggest trade deal' ever, and he pledged closer defence cooperation. He gave no terms. Philippine Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez said nothing had been signed and that the US had offered help diversifying food and energy supplies, the Daily Guardian reports. Marcos said the Pax Silica framework would not be signed on this trip.
items.notes: PBS NewsHour describes Trump as having 'signed' a deal with the Philippines, but the Philippine ambassador says nothing was signed.

items.text: Bahrain and Kuwait said they repelled air attacks on Wednesday, and Iran's army said it targeted Patriot air-defence systems at Kuwait's Ali Al-Salem air base, which hosts US forces, CBS News reports. A UAE ADNOC vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and 11 injured. CENTCOM said no US personnel were hurt in this week's attacks. CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper met Israel's military chief in Tel Aviv, and Haaretz reports that Israel is seeking US backing for renewed strikes on Iran. Three US carrier strike groups are in the region.
items.notes: The Qeshm strike was partly covered on Nov 18. Iranian state media says it caused no serious damage. The Haaretz link is paywalled.

items.text: Punchbowl News reports that a government shutdown at the Dec 11 deadline is growing more likely. Speaker Johnson and Majority Leader Thune reject any deal that limits Trump's conduct of the Iran war, while Schumer and Jeffries say they need Iran language to agree. Thune called curbs on Iran-war funding 'not a realistic ask'. Rep. Rosa DeLauro favours a short stopgap into February, when Democrats will hold both chambers. Senate Democrats are split, and retiring members and some red-state senators are wary of a hardline strategy. Congress leaves for Thanksgiving after this week and returns Nov 30.
items.notes: ABC/AP report a separate House GOP push for a $95bn package for the Iran war and Trump's priorities, but that article could not be read. The Washington Times (right-leaning) frames Democrats as debating how to block the funding without a shutdown.

items.text: The Justice Department filed an emergency application on Wednesday asking the Supreme Court, for the third time, to halt a ruling by US District Judge Edward Chen that restores Temporary Protected Status for Venezuelans. The ruling is due to take effect Friday. The administration says reinstatement would block up to 332 removal orders, force it to issue work permits, and could free about 1,800 detained Venezuelans, Al Jazeera reports. The Biden administration had extended TPS for about 600,000 Venezuelans, and the Supreme Court paused an earlier Chen ruling in 2025.
items.notes: The Washington Post (AP) link is paywalled.

items.text: US District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended by 14 days, to Dec 3, the temporary restraining order blocking construction of Trump's memorial arch at Memorial Circle in Washington, the AP reports. She said nothing material had changed since her Nov 5 order. The extension holds until Dec 3 or until she rules on a pending preliminary-injunction request, whichever comes first. The administration argues that Congress long ago authorised a monument at the site, while plaintiffs say new congressional approval is needed.
items.notes: This is a separate case from the East Potomac Park TRO before Judge Reyes (W-261116-02).

items.text: In a communiqué on Nov 18 (reported by PAP), the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) General Assembly convened by Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska said it had lifted TK President Bogdan Święczkowski's immunity in four cases: repeated delegation of nine prosecutors while he was National Prosecutor, abuse linked to the Pegasus investigation, blocking five judges from adjudicating, and an alleged physical assault on Judge Maciej Berek on Oct 14. It refused consent to detain or arrest him, but suspended him from duties and cut his pay by 50%. It also allowed the prosecution of Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański (blocking judges, violating employee rights), suspending him with a 25% pay cut. Prosecutor General Waldemar Żurek wrote that charges can now be brought; Święczkowski said no valid assembly took place, he is not suspended, he will not answer summonses, and the 'legitimate' judges will work 'in exile' for a time.
items.notes: Six judges, including Sochański, Piotrowicz and Wyrembak, say the assembly was unauthorised and inquorate (nczas.info, right-leaning). Supreme Court First President Kapiński said the law is broken 'at every step'. No vote count was published in the sources read. No attempt to detain Święczkowski was reported.

items.text: Three combined Supreme Court chambers (Civil; Labour and Social Insurance; Extraordinary Control and Public Affairs), with more than 40 judges mostly appointed after 2017, adopted a resolution on Nov 18 on a question from Civil Chamber President Joanna Misztal-Konecka. It says a valid TK ruling is one issued by a panel made up only of judges who took their oath before the President, and that such rulings are binding even if the government does not publish them in the official journal. Prawo.pl notes about 85 TK rulings remain unpublished, and five of the eight new TK judges took their oath in the Sejm, not before the President. Deputy Justice Minister Dariusz Mazur called the reports disinformation, arguing that people not entitled to sit as Supreme Court judges cannot change the law.
items.notes: TVN24 stresses that most of the judges are KRS appointees after 2017, which the government does not recognise. Right-leaning headlines (DoRzeczy, Tysol) call it a breakthrough that undermines the 'takeover' of the TK; those full articles could not be fetched. Justice Minister Żurek also rejected it, per the PAP Biznes digest.

items.text: The second round of talks on the TK crisis, chaired by the President's chief of staff Zbigniew Bogucki, took place on Nov 18 with PiS, PSL, Polska 2050, Konfederacja, Razem, Rozwój Plus, Konfederacja Korony Polskiej and Demokracja Bezpośrednia; KO and the Left again stayed away. Bogucki said the parties agree on about 70% of issues in a joint Chancellery draft constitutional amendment, based on PSL's proposal and supplemented by other clubs. He said the remaining 30%, the transitional measures to end the crisis, may be the hardest part. A third meeting is set for Thursday Nov 19 at 18:00.
items.notes: An amendment needs a two-thirds Sejm majority, which is not reachable without KO. Earlier TVN24 coverage quoted Left MP Tomasz Trela saying one does not negotiate with 'constitutional terrorists'. No draft text has been published.

items.text: Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed a Rzeczpospolita report that, in late October and early November, Polish special services, police and elite army units ran a secret preventive and deterrent operation that foiled a planned Russian sabotage provocation near the border with Russia's Kaliningrad region. Speaking in Jarosław on Nov 18, he said the services knew of the preparations and that many sabotage attempts have been foiled. He warned that Russia could also stage provocations on the Baltic states' borders, and announced a request to the PM and the President to extend Operation Horyzont, in which the army helps protect infrastructure including railways.
items.notes: The nature and location of the planned provocation were not disclosed. The original Rzeczpospolita investigation is paywalled; TVN24 and other outlets carried the PAP account.

items.text: President Nawrocki vetoed a law that would have raised VAT from 5% (8% in gastronomy) to 23% on energy drinks with caffeine or taurine, 0.0% beer, drinks up to 0.5% alcohol, and non-alcoholic alternatives containing at least 20% juice. Money.pl puts the lost revenue at about 1.3bn zł in 2027 and 15.8bn zł over 2027–2036. He signed the excise amendment raising duties on alcohol, beer, wine, intermediate products and cider from 2027, with the extra money guaranteed for the NFZ health fund as he had requested. The PAP Biznes digest says he also signed a law scrapping the internet tax relief, expanding the blood-donor relief and extending the robotisation relief by a decade.
items.thread: Poland public finances and credit ratings
items.notes: Farmer.pl reports that the President cited signals from farmers and fruit growers (juice-based drinks); not read in full. The PIT-relief signing is single-source (PAP Biznes digest via Strefa Inwestorów); TVP Info says three laws were signed in total.

items.text: On Nov 18 the Sejm Health Committee recommended rejecting four Senate amendments to the anti-alcohol law: allowing 0% beer advertising (2 for, 26 against), craft-beer events on wine-event terms, airport and free-zone exemptions from the 22:00–06:00 night sales ban, and advertising in wholesale and liquor stores. It backed allowing sponsorship information at sports events (not school sports clubs), a clarified definition of promotion, selling off non-compliant packaging, moving entry into force from Jan 1 to Jun 1, 2027, and extending the deadline for removing logos from fridges to end-2030. The Health Ministry opposed the rejected amendments. The Sejm votes during the current sitting.
items.notes: Rejecting a Senate amendment needs an absolute majority in the Sejm. The voting block is Nov 19, 10:45–13:00.

items.text: The Sejm Health Committee on Nov 18 rejected a Senate amendment cutting the minimum employment needed at a facility from half to a quarter of a full-time post, but backed the Senate's removal of sanctions (up to an 8-year ban from public-system work) for doctors who falsify records, prescriptions or sick notes. The Sejm votes on Nov 19. The bill caps pay in 2027 at about 247 zł gross an hour and a total of about 79.2k zł a month (16 times the minimum wage), with a 320-hour monthly limit. The committee chair flagged a possible presidential veto on constitutional grounds.
items.notes: Razem's Marcelina Zawisza opposes dropping the sanctions, so the floor outcome is uncertain.

items.text: UOKiK, the competition and consumer authority, fined Allegro 54.73m zł for greenwashing: 29.85m zł over its Allegro One 'one tree for 10 parcels' promise and 24.88m zł for not properly disclosing the conditions. UOKiK found that some trees were planted based on forecasts or before customers were assigned to them, and some were never planted. Customers also had to collect 10 parcels within a calendar year and, from 2024, submit a tree dedication through a panel option that was long disabled. The decision is appealable.
items.notes: No Allegro response or appeal decision was found in the sources read. The same day, Allegro raised its maximum buyback price to 65 zł a share.

items.text: The National Prosecutor's Office charged three more people in the Zondacrypto (formerly BitBay) crypto-exchange case after the CBZC cybercrime bureau detained them on Nov 17, and asked the Warsaw-Mokotów court to remand them. According to spokeswoman Anna Adamiak, they are a lawyer accused of preparing reports with false information on how client assets were secured, a former finance director accused of approving unauthorised transfers from client funds, and former BitBay co-shareholder Jacek R., who ran IT and allegedly gave unauthorised people access to user accounts. Each faces charges including membership of an organised criminal group; none admitted guilt.
items.notes: The sources give no total loss or number of victims.

items.text: Energy Minister Miłosz Motyka said on Nov 18 that a draft raising the share of gas that must be sold on the commodity exchange from 55% to 80% is at the final stage before the government's Standing Committee and may be adopted this year. He said the aim is a more transparent market, linked to lower transmission charges. He also said proposals to shield households from higher 2027 electricity bills will come in the coming weeks. ING estimates that freezing both gas and electricity prices for 2027 would cut average inflation by about 0.7 percentage points.
items.notes: The ING figure and the electricity remarks come from the PAP Biznes digest.

items.text: Eurostat data show Poland's HICP inflation eased to 3.7% year on year in October from 4.0%. According to PAP Biznes, NBP First Deputy President Marta Kightley told the Sejm that the supply shock is self-limiting but rate hikes could be used to anchor inflation expectations, and MPC member Marcin Zarzecki said the Council may be forced to hike in Q1 2027. MPC member Ireneusz Dąbrowski saw no need for hikes, citing the November NBP projection of inflation returning to target.
items.notes: Bankier's Kightley article could not be fetched; the MPC quotes rely on the digest.

items.text: Joint Sejm committees suspended work on an MPs' bill (print 3295) from Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski and Marshal Włodzimierz Czarzasty. It would move a one-off 1.5bn zł from defence spending to the Polish Science Fund to build domestic chip production lines, including at the CEZAMAT facility. The Defence Ministry said it cannot spare the money in 2026 or 2027, and the rapporteur filed many amendments the Legislative Bureau had no time to review. MPs said the coalition must first agree on funding; no new committee date is set. The bill targets 3bn zł of investment by 2030 and doubling chip specialists to about 3,000.
items.notes: Conflict: the PAP Biznes evening digest (Strefa Inwestorów, Nov 18) says the semiconductor bill 'passed committee'. Nauka w Polsce (PAP, Nov 18) and CyberDefence24 say work was suspended; the more detailed accounts are used here.

items.text: The Grudziądz city office said on Nov 18 that residents can use ePUAP again after the nationwide shutdown that followed the foreign cyberattack. The government says restoration is phased, and some functions may stay unavailable until maintenance ends. No new national statement from the Digital Affairs Ministry on full restoration, attribution or the ABW investigation was found for Nov 18.
items.notes: Local source only; treat as a sign of partial national restoration, not a confirmation. No new information on the Autopay breach (number affected) was found.

items.text: PM Donald Tusk will represent Poland at Thursday's (Nov 19) Berlin meeting of the 'coalition of the willing' convened by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, with Volodymyr Zelensky, Alexander Stubb and Andrej Babiš among those attending. The agenda covers aid to Ukraine, post-war security guarantees and coordinating the peace talks; US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected in Berlin. Poland is part of a new European negotiating team agreed in Dublin and represented by Robert Kupiecki; the Kremlin says it has not accepted European participation.
items.notes: Preview article; the meeting's outcome is due later on Nov 19.
